what_this_is: The frozen prompt protocol. A result is not a result without the protocol version attached, and the version is a label for this file's canonical hash. This file is data rather than code so that its hash means something: a refactor changes code bytes without changing what is sent, and a hash that breaks for that reason is indistinguishable from one that breaks because the protocol was altered.
how_it_changes: Never in place. A change means prompt-protocol-v2.json and a new registration naming --supersedes, so both records survive and every transcript already written still names the protocol that produced it.

envelope.shape: a single user turn whose content is the query text verbatim, and nothing else
envelope.note: No preamble, no framing, no restatement, no examples. The query text is what sample/ fixed and register/ hashed, and altering it here would mean the registered set is not the set that was asked.

system_prompt.text: When you rely on a case, give its citation.
system_prompt.rationale: citationrecord.org permits no system prompt beyond what is needed to elicit citations. This is the shortest text that does that. It deliberately does not ask for pinpoint pages, a particular citation format, a jurisdiction, or a confidence statement: whether systems supply pinpoints unprompted is one of the things being measured, and an instruction to supply them would measure the instruction instead.
system_prompt.identical_across_systems_because: A per-vendor system prompt would make the systems incomparable, which is the one thing a comparison cannot survive.

conversation_rule.note: A fresh request per query-system pair. Nothing is carried, reused or warmed between them, so no answer can be shaped by an answer that came before it.

retrieval.note: Each adapter names the exact request setting that disables retrieval, and that string is recorded on every transcript. An absence is not a declaration: a reader must be able to check the claim against the stored request rather than trust the word 'raw'.

never_retried: a response truncated at the output ceiling
retry_policy.why: None of the retryable failures carries a response from a model. Everything a model says is final and is recorded as it arrived, because a re-roll of an answer somebody did not like is the exact failure this benchmark exists to detect in others.

response_handling.note: The complete response body is stored verbatim. The assistant turn is additionally extracted by field access into the vendor's JSON envelope, never by pattern matching, and the raw body is kept regardless. If a model returns something malformed, that is data.

sampling_policy.principle: Record what was requested, what was actually sent, and what the vendor does not accept, as three separate things.
sampling_policy.why: A benchmark that believed it had set temperature everywhere, and had not, would carry a hole nothing later could find. The three systems below do not share a sampling surface and no wording can make them.
sampling_policy.comparability: There is no single temperature for this edition. The per-system table below is the honest form and is published with the edition.

sampling.note: Claude Opus 5 does not accept temperature, top_p or top_k; they were removed with the adaptive-thinking models and the API returns 400. There is no temperature to record, and writing temperature: 0 into a provenance record because this protocol asked for one would be a false statement.

claude.extra_note: Sent explicitly rather than left to the default so that the request bytes state the setting instead of relying on a documented default that may change. Thinking is left on: a model with thinking disabled is not the model anyone uses, and whether it matters is a thing to find out rather than to assume.

sampling.note: The reasoning models restrict these to their default values and reject others. Nothing is sent rather than sending a value that would be ignored or refused.
Accepts temperature. Set to 0, which is what the other two would carry if they accepted it.

grok.scope_note: Not in the published scope of Edition One. Run in the pilot to find out whether it differs enough from the other three to be worth changing the page, which is a question the pilot answers and this protocol does not.

model_identifiers.note: The identifier above is what is asked for. What the API reports back is recorded beside it, because they can differ, and a vendor silently serving a different snapshot than the one requested is itself a finding that is invisible unless both are written down.

what_this_protocol_does_not_do: It does not assess. Nothing in runner/ classifies, scores, ranks or flags any response, and no field of a transcript can hold a judgment. Counting citations, extracting propositions and every other reading of a response happens afterwards, separately, over stored files.
